requests.what: Several kinds of record are filed under INT-FSIM-01 (BD-006/BD-007's five crates with the cold check; N33a-12's bedrock record; the M1 first-use records of N33a-15, -16, -19, -30, N33a-17's ledger record, N33a-31's at M3; N33a-20's FD-FSCI record, as the ledger row says; N33a-10 already lists these kinds). Two rules break on that: (1) rule 8 `measured-missing` requires every threshold of the gate's row (cold check <= 3600 s) on each record, so every bedrock and first-use record is invalid; (2) `admitted_gates` and the status table use 'the newest record per gate', so a newer failing first-use record makes INT-FSIM-01 read as not passed and flips N33a-03's check_admitted. Suggested: rule 8 applies the row's thresholds to records whose covers equal the gate's own; any other record under the gate needs at least one measured known answer with its threshold; 'newest record per gate' means per (gate, covers) set, and admitted_gates reads the gate's own covers.

Never-inherited step 1 counts every foundation crate in the resolved graph as a use. A group feature compiles its whole closure: the M1 set compiles 65 FrankenSim crates while the M0 and M1 records name about thirty, and the bedrock record covers 10 of a 16-crate closure; from M1, frob-arena enables `optimize` for fs-eproc (BD-124), which compiles fs-dfo, fs-bo, fs-ascent, fs-archive, fs-opt, fs-sos, fs-tropical and fs-symmetry, first used at M3 to M4 (N33a-31, N33bx-03). check-stack would then report unadmitted-use for dozens of crates and fail at M0 and M1. A use should be a crate an enabled airlock trait reaches directly (a per-trait crate list in N33a-11's group registry) plus the bedrock-direct crates, with transitive crates covered by the record of the crate that pulls them in; or N33a-11 splits `optimize` so Racing has its own feature.

Its acceptance runs `frob sim run --tier referee --fixture traction/<name> …`, but the --fixture input and the fixture registry are N24b-03's (VERBS-sim's --fixture row, owner N24b-03 at M1), and N24b-03 depends on BD-080 (via BD-122, BD-121, N24a-11, BD-094), so BD-080 cannot pass those items until a bead that depends on it lands (convention 7). Either move the CLI items to a bead that depends on both (N33ap1-01 now asserts the riser-edge object end to end and depends on N24b-03) or have BD-080 assert through its in-process fixtures only.

Its probe known answers (and N32b-11's tests) use g = 9.81: a 2 kg box gives 19.62 N, the 20-degree incline 18.44 N and 6.71 N. The program's convention is standard gravity 9.80665 m/s² (N13-07, BD-080, BD-117), which gives 19.6133 N, 18.4307 N and 6.7081 N. The step asserts the dequantized value within one quantum plus the solver's contact tolerance of the closed form, so a correct overlay on a standard-gravity scene can fail by 0.0067 N. Either state g = 9.81 in the analytic scenes' files or use 9.80665 in the closed forms (BD-300 restates N32b-11's figures and follows whichever holds).
